name: Classic Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: A simple, authentic Italian pasta dish made with garlic, olive oil, and chilli flakes. Ready in under 20 minutes with pantry staples.

steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add spaghetti and cook according to package directions until al dente (8-10 minutes). Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and cook gently for 3-4 minutes until golden (not browned).
Add chilli flakes to the garlic oil and stir for 30 seconds.
Add drained pasta to the skillet along with a splash of reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify the sauce and coat the pasta evenly.
Remove from heat. Add chopped parsley, season with salt and black pepper, and serve immediately.
steps.tip: The pasta water starch is the secret to a silky sauce.

cooking_tips: Do not let garlic burn — keep heat medium-low.
Reserve pasta water before draining, as it is essential to the sauce.
Use good quality extra-virgin olive oil for best flavour.

name: Masala Omelette
description: A spiced Indian-style omelette packed with onions, tomatoes, green chilli, and coriander. A quick protein-rich breakfast or light meal.

steps.instruction: Finely chop onion, tomato, green chilli, and coriander.
Beat eggs in a bowl. Add all chopped vegetables, turmeric, cumin, and salt. Mix well.
Heat oil/butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour egg mixture and spread evenly.
Cook for 2 minutes until edges set. Fold in half or roll, cook another minute, and serve hot.
steps.tip: Cover with a lid for 1 minute for a fluffier omelette.

cooking_tips: Use fresh eggs for a fluffier omelette.
Medium heat prevents burning.
Add cheese for a richer version.

name: Chicken Stir-Fry with Vegetables
description: A fast, flavourful stir-fry with tender chicken, colourful vegetables, and a savoury soy-ginger sauce. Perfect weeknight dinner.

steps.instruction: Slice chicken breast thinly. Toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch. Let marinate 5 minutes.
Cut all vegetables into bite-sized pieces. Mince garlic and ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Stir-fry chicken for 4-5 minutes until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add carrots and broccoli, cook 3 minutes. Add bell pepper, cook 2 more minutes.
Return chicken to pan. Add remaining soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss everything together for 1 minute. Garnish with spring onion and serve over rice.
steps.tip: Keep heat high throughout for best texture.

substitutions.effect_on_recipe: tamari is gluten-free; coconut aminos is milder

substitutions.substitute: bok choy, cabbage, or green beans

cooking_tips: High heat is essential for a proper stir-fry.
Prep all ingredients before you start cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan.

name: Lentil Dal
description: A hearty, nourishing Indian red lentil dal with warming spices. Naturally vegan, high in protein and fibre, and ready in 30 minutes.

steps.instruction: Rinse lentils until water runs clear. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pot. Add cumin seeds and let sizzle 30 seconds. Add diced onion and cook 5 minutes until golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute. Add diced tomatoes and cook 3-4 minutes until soft.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. Stir well.
Add rinsed lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes until lentils are completely soft and dal has thickened.
Stir in garam masala. Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or flatbread.
steps.tip: Add a squeeze of lemon before serving for brightness.

substitutions.substitute: yellow split peas or green lentils
substitutions.quantity_guidance: same amount; increase cooking time by 10 minutes

cooking_tips: Rinse lentils thoroughly to remove excess starch.
Dal thickens as it cools; add a little water when reheating.
A tadka (tempered spices in hot oil) poured on top at serving elevates the dish.

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
description: Creamy smashed avocado on toasted sourdough topped with a perfectly poached egg. A nutritious, trendy breakfast or brunch dish.

steps.instruction: Toast the sourdough slices until golden and crisp.
Halve avocado, remove stone, scoop flesh into a bowl. Add lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mash roughly with a fork.
Bring a small saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Add white vinegar. Crack egg into a small cup. Create a gentle swirl in the water and slide the egg in. Poach for 3 minutes for a runny yolk.
Spread smashed avocado on toast. Top with poached egg. Season with salt, pepper, and chilli flakes. Serve immediately.
steps.tip: Fresh eggs hold together better when poaching.

substitutions.substitute: any bread, rye, or whole wheat
lime juice or a splash of vinegar

cooking_tips: Use ripe avocados for the creamiest spread.
The water for poaching should be barely simmering, not boiling.
Add feta or microgreens for extra flavour.

name: Tomato Basil Soup
description: A velvety, warming tomato soup with fresh basil and a touch of cream. Simple pantry ingredients, beautiful result.

steps.instruction: Dice onion and roughly chop tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot. Cook onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add garlic, cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook 10 minutes until tomatoes break down.
Pour in vegetable stock and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add fresh basil. Use an immersion blender to blend until smooth. Stir in cream.
steps.tip: Blend carefully; hot liquids expand.

steps.instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with crusty bread and a drizzle of olive oil.

cooking_tips: A pinch of sugar balances tomato acidity.
Roasting tomatoes first adds deeper flavour.
Pair with grilled cheese for a classic combination.

name: Mushroom Fried Rice
description: Umami-packed fried rice with mushrooms, eggs, and vegetables. Uses leftover rice for a quick and satisfying meal.

steps.instruction: Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic. Slice spring onion.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Beat eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble quickly. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil. Stir-fry garlic 30 seconds. Add mushrooms and cook 3 minutes.
Add cold cooked rice. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry on high heat for 3-4 minutes until slightly crispy.
steps.tip: Day-old cold rice gives the best texture.

steps.instruction: Add soy sauce, white pepper, and scrambled eggs. Toss together. Finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

cooking_tips: Use day-old rice for best texture.
High heat is essential for fried rice.
Add a splash of water if rice sticks to the pan.

name: Black Bean Tacos
description: Smoky, satisfying black bean tacos with fresh salsa and lime. A quick, budget-friendly Mexican-inspired dinner.

steps.instruction: Make salsa: finely dice tomato and half the onion. Mix with lime juice, chopped coriander, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Drain and rinse black beans. Dice remaining onion. Mince garlic.
Heat oil in a pan. Cook onion 3 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute.
Add beans to pan. Mash lightly with a fork. Cook 3-4 minutes, adding a splash of water if too dry. Season with salt.
Warm tortillas in a dry pan. Spoon beans onto tortillas, top with fresh salsa. Serve with lime wedges.
steps.tip: Add sliced avocado, sour cream, or hot sauce as desired.

cooking_tips: Warm tortillas properly to prevent cracking.
A pinch of smoked paprika adds depth to the beans.
Top with sliced avocado for richness.

name: Greek Salad
description: A refreshing classic Greek salad with tomatoes, cucumber, olives, red onion, and creamy feta. Light, healthy, no cooking required.

steps.instruction: Cut tomatoes into wedges. Slice cucumber into thick half-moons. Thinly slice red onion.
Combine tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Drizzle dressing over salad. Top with crumbled or sliced feta. Serve immediately.
steps.tip: Do not toss vigorously — Greek salad is gently mixed.

cooking_tips: Use ripe tomatoes for best flavour.
Soak sliced red onion in cold water for 10 minutes to reduce sharpness.
Add a small amount of lemon zest to the dressing for extra brightness.

name: Banana Oat Pancakes
description: Fluffy, naturally sweet pancakes made from ripe bananas and oats. Gluten-free, dairy-free, and quick to prepare for a wholesome breakfast.

steps.instruction: Blend oats in a blender until flour-like. Add bananas, eggs, baking powder, cinnamon, and vanilla. Blend until smooth.
Let batter rest 2 minutes.
steps.tip: The batter should be thick but pourable. Add 1-2 tbsp water if too thick.

steps.instruction: Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat with a little oil/butter. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook 2-3 minutes until bubbles form, then flip and cook 1-2 more minutes.
Serve stacked with honey or maple syrup, fresh fruit, or nut butter.

substitutions.substitute: flax eggs (1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water per egg)

cooking_tips: Riper bananas = sweeter pancakes.
Keep heat on medium-low to cook through without burning.
These pancakes are fragile; flip gently.

name: Creamy Butter Chicken
description: Rich, aromatic Indian butter chicken with a velvety tomato-cream sauce. A restaurant-quality curry made at home.

steps.instruction: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, turmeric, and chilli powder. Set aside.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Brown chicken pieces for 5-6 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, melt remaining butter. Cook diced onion 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Add garam masala, cumin, and coriander powder. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomato passata. Stir well and simmer 10 minutes.
Return browned chicken to sauce. Simmer 10 minutes until cooked through. Stir in cream. Adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or naan.
steps.tip: A knob of butter stirred in at the end gives extra richness.

cooking_tips: Use chicken thighs for juicier results.
Do not rush the sauce — simmering develops deeper flavour.
Serve with basmati rice or naan bread.

name: Vegetable Minestrone Soup
description: A hearty Italian vegetable soup loaded with seasonal vegetables, beans, and pasta in a rich tomato broth. Nourishing, filling, and flexible.

steps.instruction: Dice onion, carrot, celery, and zucchini. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot. Cook onion, carrot, and celery 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add zucchini, canned tomatoes, thyme, and oregano. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a boil. Add beans and simmer 10 minutes.
Add pasta and cook according to package time (usually 8-10 minutes). Season with salt and pepper. Serve with crusty bread.
steps.tip: Add a Parmesan rind to the stock for extra depth (non-vegan).

substitutions.substitute: chickpeas, kidney beans, or borlotti beans

cooking_tips: Use whatever vegetables you have.
Cook pasta separately and add to bowls to prevent it becoming soggy when storing leftovers.
Minestrone is even better the next day.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a richly spiced tomato and pepper sauce. A popular Middle Eastern breakfast or brunch dish.

steps.instruction: Dice onion and red bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet. Cook onion and bell pepper over medium heat for 7 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli powder. Stir 1 minute.
Add canned tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well. Cover pan and cook 6-8 minutes until whites are set but yolks remain runny. Garnish with parsley. Serve with pita or crusty bread.
steps.tip: Do not overcook the eggs; they continue cooking off heat.

cooking_tips: Use a wide pan so eggs fit without overlapping.
The sauce should be thick before adding eggs.
Top with crumbled feta for a richer version.

name: Classic Margherita Pizza
description: A homemade Margherita pizza with a thin, crispy base, fresh tomato sauce, and melted mozzarella. Authentic Italian flavours from scratch.

steps.instruction: Mix flour, yeast, and salt. Add warm water and olive oil. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Make sauce: blend canned tomatoes with garlic, olive oil, and salt. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Preheat oven to maximum temperature (250°C/480°F). Place a baking tray in the oven to heat.
steps.tip: A hot oven is essential for crispy pizza.

steps.instruction: Stretch dough into a thin round on a floured surface. Transfer to baking paper.
Spread sauce over base. Tear and distribute mozzarella. Season with salt.
Slide pizza (with paper) onto hot tray. Bake 12-15 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly. Top with fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil before serving.

cooking_tips: Maximum oven temperature is key.
Do not overload with toppings.
Rest dough before stretching for easier handling.

name: Hummus with Pita
description: Silky smooth homemade hummus with tahini and lemon. A nutritious, versatile snack or mezze served with warm pita bread.

steps.instruction: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Reserve a few for garnish.
Blend tahini and lemon juice together in a food processor for 1 minute until creamy.
Add garlic, cumin, and a pinch of salt. Blend 30 seconds.
Add chickpeas. Blend 2 minutes, slowly adding ice water until smooth and creamy.
steps.tip: Ice water makes hummus noticeably silkier.

steps.instruction: Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in a bowl, drizzled with olive oil, a sprinkle of paprika, and reserved chickpeas. Warm pita bread and serve.

substitutions.substitute: peanut butter or sunflower seed butter
lime juice or white wine vinegar

cooking_tips: Blend for a full 2 minutes for the smoothest hummus.
Ice water is the secret to creamy hummus.
Homemade hummus keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days.

name: Salmon Teriyaki
description: Glazed salmon fillet with a sweet-savoury teriyaki sauce. Restaurant-quality result at home in under 20 minutes.

steps.instruction: Mix soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, minced garlic, ginger, and sesame oil together to make teriyaki sauce.
Pat salmon dry. Heat oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon skin-side up and cook 3 minutes.
Flip salmon. Pour teriyaki sauce over fillets. Cook 2 minutes, then place pan under a hot grill/broiler for 3-4 minutes until caramelised.
Garnish with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion. Serve with steamed rice.
steps.tip: Do not overcook salmon — it should be just opaque in the centre.

substitutions.effect_on_recipe: different texture; tofu makes it vegan

cooking_tips: Pat fish dry for a better sear.
Watch carefully under the grill as honey burns quickly.
Marinating for 15 minutes intensifies the flavour.

name: Chickpea Curry (Chana Masala)
description: A bold, fragrant Indian chickpea curry with whole spices and tangy tomatoes. Hearty, vegan, and packed with protein and flavour.

steps.instruction: Heat oil in a pot. Add cumin seeds and let sizzle 30 seconds. Add finely diced onion. Cook 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes. Cook 8-10 minutes until they break down and oil separates.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli powder, and salt. Stir well and cook 2 minutes.
Add drained chickpeas and 200ml water. Stir, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
Add garam masala and amchur. Cook 2 more minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or roti.
steps.tip: Amchur adds essential tartness — substitute with lemon juice if unavailable.

substitutions.substitute: 1 tsp lemon juice or tamarind paste

cooking_tips: Cooking onions until deep golden is essential for curry depth.
The oil separating from tomatoes indicates the masala base is ready.
Partially mash some chickpeas for a thicker sauce.

name: Caprese Salad
description: The simplest Italian salad — ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, and basil drizzled with olive oil and balsamic. No cooking required.

steps.instruction: Slice tomatoes and mozzarella into even rounds.
Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a serving plate.
steps.tip: Slightly overlapping slices looks most attractive.

steps.instruction: Tuck fresh basil leaves between slices.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper. Serve immediately.

substitutions.substitute: balsamic glaze or red wine vinegar

cooking_tips: Only use the ripest tomatoes available.
Good olive oil makes all the difference.
Serve at room temperature, not straight from the fridge.

name: French Onion Soup
description: Classic deeply caramelised onion soup topped with crusty croutons and melted gruyère. A French bistro staple that takes patience but rewards it.

steps.instruction: Thinly slice all onions. Heat butter and olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat. Add onions and a pinch of salt.
Cook onions slowly for 40-50 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes, until deeply golden and caramelised. This step cannot be rushed.
steps.tip: Low and slow is the secret. Do not turn up the heat.

steps.instruction: Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute. Pour in white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan. Cook until wine evaporates.
Add stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes. Remove thyme and bay leaf. Adjust seasoning.
Toast baguette slices. Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls. Top with baguette slices and grated gruyère. Grill/broil until cheese is melted and bubbling.

substitutions.substitute: extra stock or apple cider vinegar
substitutions.effect_on_recipe: deglazes the pan; skip wine if preferred

cooking_tips: Do not rush the caramelisation — 40 minutes minimum.
A heavy-bottomed pot prevents burning.
Adding a pinch of sugar speeds up caramelisation slightly.

name: Overnight Oats
description: No-cook oats soaked overnight in milk with chia seeds and honey. A quick, nutritious, meal-prep breakfast ready in the morning.

steps.instruction: Combine oats, milk, yoghurt, chia seeds, honey, and vanilla in a jar or container. Stir well.
Seal and refrigerate overnight (at least 4 hours).
steps.tip: Can be prepared up to 3 days ahead.

steps.instruction: In the morning, stir and add a splash of milk if too thick. Top with fresh berries or sliced banana and serve.

substitutions.substitute: oat milk, almond milk, or coconut milk

cooking_tips: Use rolled oats, not instant, for best texture.
Chia seeds thicken the oats overnight.
Add nut butter for extra protein and richness.
